Peter Stanley |from=Mountain View, CA |other_entries=[[Tantrum]], [[Blip]] |weapons=2x Vertical spinners |associated=[[Insult and Injury]] (Aren Hill) |live=BattleBots Proving Ground (2023) |other_events=BattleBots Pro League (2026)|stats=The_Twins_stats.png}}'''The Twins''' is a [[Heavyweights|heavyweight]] designed by [[Seems Reasonable Robotics]], which debuted in ''[[BattleBots]]'' [[BattleBots Proving Ground|''Proving Ground'']] and has since fought in the 2026 ''[[BattleBots Pro League]]''.

A third ''BattleBots'' entry from Aren Hill's [[Giant Nut]]-winning team, The Twins is a two-part [[Multibots|multibot]] consisting of identical, four-wheel drive robots armed with 24lb [[Vertical Spinners|vertical spinners]]. The design is an upscaled version of the team's 3lb multibot '''Twerps''', which competed in the ''National Havoc Robot League'' event in March 2023, among other smaller robots from Seems Reasonable Robotics' respective team members. Each Twin is identifiable by codes written on their sides reading '''UNIT-01''' and '''UNIT-02'''.

Each Twin boasts the same drivetrain which led Tantrum to championship success in 2021 and has six magnets fitted to their underside for additional downforce and drive power comparable to [[Claw Viper]], according to Aren Hill.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LkPU46ihemE Green Square Talks Battlebots: Proving Grounds Review Part 3 (w/ Disarray and The Twins)] Aren Hill revealed the concept for The Twins in Episode 74 of the combat robotics podcast ''Outside of the Box'', released in March 2023.https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZnsRNdCs_ts&t=1381s Its drivers were originally unconfirmed, with Tantrum's co-captains ruling themselves out of this role. Alex Grant admitted he had never driven one of the team's heavyweights before in battle and Ginger Schmidt stated that driving did not appeal to her either. However, he would later confirm the drivers to be himself and William Stanley for The Twins' debut in an episode of ''Green Square Talks BattleBots''. The robots' renders were revealed in August 2023, though the team stated their initial fights would serve to test functionality above anything else, and the final design may still vary. Seems Reasonable Robotics brought The Twins to ''BattleBots'' ''Proving Ground'' in September 2023, where the multibot took on [[Fireball]], captained by [[Bots 'n' Stuff Robotics]] member Brian Boxell. Despite a promising showing, The Twins lost by knockout. {{Quote|We'll dial in aesthetics after we finalize the robot geometry for S8, it'll get it's glow up (or people will fall in love with the current look and we'll run with it).|Alex Grant in the ''NHRL'' Discord serverhttps://discord.com/channels/651601084019900483/809971550937808926/1145810619979808868}}It is also uncertain what the debut of The Twins may mean for the team's current robots - [[Tantrum]] and [[Blip]]. Aren Hill revealed in January 2024 that The Twins would "probably" return to ''Proving Ground'' in the future, stating his desire to fight one of the leading spinners in the field, but he was unable to commit to another weekend of fights until World Championship VIII filming dates were announced. Following struggles to get ''BattleBots'' picked up by a TV network, The Twins were revealed to be Seems Reasonable Robotics' sole entry into the upcoming [[BattleBots Pro League|''BattleBots Pro League'']] in early 2026. The Twins now featured additional armor with purple accents as well as options for forks rather than piano key wedgelets or a plow at the front. New also for this competition, each Twin has a dedicated [[Self-righting mechanism|self-righting arm]].[https://youtu.be/jkdQU7GUxh0?si=TqlIPmGNtl3K_Vbt&t=434 BATTLEBOTS IS BACK!] The team produced four individual Twin machines for the competition, as well as spares for two additional bots. Aren Hill remained one of the two drivers, with Dillon Carey driving the other in place of William Stanley. This meant Blip and Tantrum's designated drivers were at the controls of The Twins for this event. The_Twins_low_shot_Pro_League.jpg|An alternative shot of The Twins. '''The Twins vs. Fireball (9/9/2023)'''

[[File:The-Twins-vs-Fireball-Tile-1024x1024.png|left|thumb|The Twins vs. Fireball, as advertised on the ''BattleBots'' website.]]The Twins made their debut during the September 9, 2023 [[BattleBots Proving Ground|''Proving Ground'']] show, where took on [[Fireball]].

[[File:Fireball vs The Twins.png|thumb|The Twins look to confuse Fireball.]]Immediately, The Twins split off to occupy different areas of the [[BattleBox]], each getting their vertical spinners up to speed. Fireball manoeuvred around to set its sights on one of the Twins, riding up its wedge momentarily but slipping away before both weapons made contact.

[[File:Fireball vs The Twins 1.gif|left|thumb|A Twin tears off Fireball's fork before being struck by its vertical spinner.]]Fireball then drove up the front of the same Twin, losing its left fork as a result. The 125lb bot remained close, but was struck by the vertical spinner of Fireball and was sent into a frontflip, peeling up part of its armor but landing on its wheels. The other Twin then took the reigns, striking the side of Fireball and causing its remaining fork to become jammed in an upright position.

[[File:Fireball vs The Twins 2.gif|thumb|Fireball throws itself over.]]Looking to confuse Brian Boxell, The Twins kept their distance and allowed Fireball to drive between them before closing in to attack together. Fireball escaped, but lifted up on one side as its anti-gyro flywheel appeared non-functional and landed upside-down. One of the Twins looked to capitalize and hit the side of Fireball, who used the BattleBox to right itself.

[[File:Fireball vs The Twins 3.gif|left|thumb|One half of the multibot becomes incapacitated.]]The Twins then returned to the center of the arena, but as one half met Fireball head on, it was the 250lb bot which won the ground game and sent the Twin into a backflip, following this up with an attack which sent it bouncing away into the screws. Though it recovered from the hazard, that one Twin appeared to now be struggling to drive on one side, and its piano key forks had been damaged. The other Twin gave chase but caught a seam in the BattleBox floor and landed upside-down.

[[File:Fireball The Twins Proving Ground.gif|thumb|Fireball punts one of the Twins through the air.]]The remaining Twin tried to help its stranded teammate, but was quickly hunted down by Fireball. With a minute to go, Fireball's vertical spinner caught the side of the 125lb bot, launching it into the screws and immobilizing the remaining Twin.
{{Dialogue a-b|Steve Judkins|It looks like one of The Twins could be out of action, Bil.|Bil Dwyer|That's why there's two of 'em! Under a minute- OHHHH!|Steve Judkins and Bil Dwyer react to both Twins being immobilized}}
With both robots out of action, a count began and Fireball took the win by knockout. |- |

'''The Twins vs. Fireball (9/10/2023)'''

The Twins was scheduled to take on [[Fireball]] for a second time during the weekend's live shows. However, Seems Reasonable Robotics opted to withdraw as they required a new nut to be machined for their weapon, and The Twins were replaced by the [[ShowBot]] version of [[Witch Doctor (ShowBot)|Witch Doctor]]. |- ! scope="col" style="text-align: center;" | === BattleBots Pro League (2026)=== |- |{{Fight Order Unknown}}

'''The Twins vs. Cobalt'''

Entering Group C of the ''BattleBots Pro League'', The Twins took seasoned competitor [[Cobalt]]. Both Twins were equipped with their hinged fork configuration to negate the forks of their opponent.

[[File:The Twins formation vs Cobalt Pro League.png|left|thumb|Both competitors enter an early stalemate.]]The multibot began the fight by immediately splitting up and going on the defensive. Twin 2 went into the shelf corner, while Twin 1 moved around the pulverizers, forcing Cobalt to split its focus. Twin 1 would continue to approach and back away from Cobalt in an attempt to engage, but Cobalt would not take the bait, preferring to stay in the shelf corner opposite Twin 2.

[[File:Cobalt The Twins Pro League.jpg|thumb|The Twins face off against Cobalt.]]Cobalt began to pursue Twin 1, before backing off again, showing intent to engage without actually making contact. As the first minute ended, Cobalt and Twin 1 lined up and faced each other down before Cobalt charged a spinning Twin 1. Twin 2 would subsequently charge in to help fight back against the larger Cobalt. The Twins successfully dodged around and avoided Cobalt's front end, before Twin 1 managed to get underneath and flip its larger opponent.

[[File:Cobalt The Twins hit Pro League.gif|left|thumb|As Cobalt slams a Twin into the Upper Deck, its partner instantly retaliates.]]Both teams seemed dazed coming out of the exchange, with Cobalt chasing after the fleeing Twin 1. Twin 2 landed a fleeting jab as Cobalt gyroed in the air, before the Twins backed Cobalt into their own pulverizer zone. They were unable to capitalize on this momentum shift as Twin 2 oversteered, presenting its side to Cobalt, which took the bot and slammed it into the shelf, launching it into the air. Twin 1 would avenge this hit by charging in immediately after and sending Cobalt itself up into the air before both Twins once again cornered Cobalt.

[[File:The Twins Cobalt Pro League last minute.jpg|thumb|One Twin crashes into Cobalt as the other watches on.]]The pair would take turns getting under and hitting Cobalt, before Twin 1 pinned Cobalt to the wall, allowing Twin 2 to take its time to score another large blow. This seemingly damaged Cobalts left side drive as The Twins continued to capitalize with additional coordinated attacks as the fight entered its last minute.

[[File:Cobalt The Twins Pro League KO.png|left|thumb|A count begins against Cobalt.]]Both Twins would make some driving errors that allowed Cobalt a few glancing blows, but at this point, only Twin 2 was needed to keep the veteran immobile as shrapnel had sliced through a power lead connected to one of Cobalt's speed controllers.[https://discord.com/channels/293793025761476611/438752241042849793/1529944407590043828 Explanation by Derek Tran in the Out of the Arena Discord server] One final shot from Twin 2 at 20 seconds left in the fight sealed the deal, as with just one second remaining, The Twins picked up their first ''BattleBots'' win by knockout - the first by a multibot in seven years. |- |
